questions.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,j \\  & =2x\,i+2y\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{t}$ and $y={e}^{-t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =2{e}^{t}\,i+2{e}^{-t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})\,j \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i-{e}^{-t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2{e}^{t}\,i+2{e}^{-t}\,j)\cdot ({e}^{t}\,i-{e}^{-t}\,j) \\  & =2{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{t}-2{e}^{-t}\cdot {e}^{-t} \\  & =2{e}^{2t}-2{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t,2t⟩$ at the point $t=\pi .$
questions.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y),\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)⟩ \\  & =⟨2x\operatorname{sin}⁡y,{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡y⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡t$ and $y=2t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,{ln}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,{ln}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩\cdot ⟨\frac{1}{t},2⟩ \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\cdot \frac{1}{t}+{ln}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡2t}{t}+2{ln}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=\pi $ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(\pi ))] & =\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi }{\pi }+2{ln}^{2}⁡\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi  \\  & =2{ln}^{2}⁡\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡xy)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡xy)\,j \\  & =\frac{y}{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,i+\frac{x}{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,j\text{ }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{t}$ and $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,i+\frac{{e}^{t}}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,i+\frac{{e}^{t}}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,j)\cdot ({e}^{t}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}+\frac{{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}{1+{e}^{2t}{sin}^{2}⁡t}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})\,j \\  & =\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,i+\frac{y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,j\text{ }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{t}$ and $y=t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}\,i+\frac{t}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}\,i+\frac{t}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}\,j)\cdot ({e}^{t}\,i+j) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}+\frac{t}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}+t}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z))\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z))\,k \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+z)\,i+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,j+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+z)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t+1,$ $y=2t$ and $z={t}^{2}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,i+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,j+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =\,i+2\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,i+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,j+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\,k)\cdot (\,i+2\,j+2t\,k) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\cdot 1+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\cdot 2+(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})\cdot 2t \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2t(t+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2(t+1)(1+t)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+{t}^{2})+2(t+1)^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+{t}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
